messages:
alex-b: heads-up — i'm sketching a tenant-level override UX for v1->v2 deprecation. want a quick sync on routing, quota accounting, and console copy. thinking per-tenant opt-in with a deferral window.

maria_s: +1. do you mean per-tenant *route* overrides (e.g. /generate: use v2) or whole-tenant pinning? big difference for billing.

alex-b: route-level preferred for flexibility but fallback to tenant-wide if they choose. main concern: double-counting tokens during gradual rollout and how quotas/budgets surface in console.

samuel: two quick asks: 1) telemetry key to know "opt-in fraction" per tenant so we can detect quality regressions; 2) signal to routing so we can drain back to v1 on errors.

nate-ops: +1 on circuit backoff. routing policy should expose a health hook. also need a hard cap for reserved tenants so they don't exceed committed throughput when they opt-in early.

maria_s: about quotas: if tenant opts some routes into v2, do we attribute tokens to v2 pricing immediately? we need a migration grace pricing flag otherwise billing will surprise customers.

alex-b: plan: console shows two numbers side-by-side for the rollout period — "billing preview (v2 rates)" and "billing actual (current)". default billing won't switch until tenant explicitly confirms after the deferral window.

samuel: can we add a sampling probe for generative quality in that window? small % of calls should be routed to v2 for eval sets, with detailed eval telemetry. sth like: sample=0.05 per route.

maria_s: that helps. what about quota enforcement? should we pro-rate quotas for mixed routing? e.g., tenant has 1M token/month; if 20% routed to v2, the effective tokens consumed against same bucket but show split.

alex-b: yes, pro-rate against same logical bucket but console will break down usage by model-version. billing switch remains a manual step.

nate-ops: operationally we need a tenant_override flag in API and console toggle. propose API: `routing_override: { scope: "route|tenant", target_version: "v1|v2", expires_at: <ts> }`

samuel: sketch of config looks fine. pls include `rollback_on_error: true` and `health_threshold_pct` for auto-fallback.

alex-b: here's a quick paste for the console copy i'm thinking: 
```
Enable tenant routing overrides
• Route-level overrides let you opt specific endpoints into v2 for testing.
• Billing preview shows estimated cost at v2 rates during the evaluation window.
• Overrides auto-expire after 7 days unless confirmed.
```

maria_s: copy looks good. add note: "Using overrides does not change billing until you confirm" — very important.

console-bot: flag created: `console.feature.tenant_override_v2` by alex-b. rollout 10% -> 50% in 2 days. docs PR: https://git.internal/r/redwood/docs/pull/812

samuel: nit: rollout ramp should be opt-in per org. ops can't assume 50% ramp for everyone. suggest default 0% and allow org-admin to pick ramp schedule.

alex-b: agreed. default to manual enable, quick preset options in UX (1%, 5%, 25%, 100%). we'll add an advanced schedule later.

nate-ops: last ops note: ensure we have a fallback trace for each routed request so we can trace which routing decision was made and why (overrides, affinity, probe). telemetry needs a `routing_reason` tag.

alex-b: noted — will add telemetry keys: `routing_decision`, `override_source`, `override_expiry`.

maria_s: ok next steps: alex to update console mockups and docs PR, sam to add sampling probe metrics, nate to wire health hook and cap enforcement, i'll draft billing preview UX copy. sync in 48h?

alex-b: SG. ping me if anything blocks. :thumbsup:

samuel: thanks — will stub telemetry in probes repo and ping this thread when ready.

nate-ops: i'll schedule a quick ops runbook for emergency rollback.

amelia: (react) :eyes:
